subject: Re: Order form redlines — derivative flagging & model reuse constraints
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia@hightower.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Patel <mark@hightower.ai>
Date: 2028-07-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Order form redlines: output entitlement & training concerns

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our legal team attached a round of redlines on the MSA + order form (Hightower_redlines_v2.docx). Primary concerns are below — can you please confirm Redwood's position and (if possible) provide suggested alternative language we can take to our GC?

1) Output ownership: We want explicit assignment of output (customer-generated content) such that Hightower has title for downstream productization. Current order form language reads like a license. Is assignment on the table?

2) Training / model reuse: Hightower requires that Redwood not use our traffic or outputs to train models outside the instance specified in the order form. We need a clear prohibition or an opt-in training flag with technical and audit guarantees.

3) Feedback license: The redline asks that any feedback be owned by Hightower or not used for improvements. We can consider a narrow telemetry/bug-fix exception but need clarity.

4) Derivative flagging & model reuse: We added a clause requesting a visible flag (metadata) on outputs that may have been influenced by third‑party proprietary prompts/data. This is important for compliance and downstream attribution.

Please see attached redlines. SOC2_summary.pdf included per procurement request. We need to get a signed order form by end of month to hit our Q4 rollout.

Can we coordinate on language today?

— Alicia
Alicia Torres
Head of Procurement, Hightower AI
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@hightower.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines: output entitlement & training concerns

Alicia — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the doc. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (sales/procurement) so we can triage quickly. High level responses before Laura adds legal wording: 

1) Output ownership: Redwood does not typically assign underlying model IP. We can offer a broad, perpetual, sublicensable license to use customer outputs for their productization purposes. If assignment is a hard requirement for Hightower, we need to understand the specific downstream use cases (e.g., resale, embedding in a product that will be sublicensed) so we can evaluate precedents and risk.

2) Training / model reuse: We can commit to a default "no-training" posture for customer traffic on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, we can surface an explicit opt-in flag and produce audit evidence (audit logs showing opt-in). We can propose the following: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to refine, train, or improve any models used to provide Services to other customers unless Customer provides explicit opt-in in writing or via the admin console."

3) Feedback license: We can limit any feedback license to anonymized, aggregated telemetry for product improvements and offer a carveout for operational bug fixes (security fixes, performance regression analysis). If Hightower insists on no-use at all, we can offer an alternate paid add-on: "redacted-feedback lockbox".

4) Derivative flagging: Technically feasible as metadata tagging on our response payloads (we can add a boolean and a provenance field). We need to confirm scope (all responses vs. those that reference third‑party data). Ben — can you confirm whether this is acceptable operationally, and if there is a deadline for the flag to be in place?

Attaching a short proposed response (RKim_proposed_response_v1.docx) with suggested redlines. Laura — could you review and propose legal text for outputs/assignment and feedback license?

Happy to jump on a 30 min call today if that helps.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior PM, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T14:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines: output entitlement & training concerns

Rachel — reviewed Alicia's redlines and your proposed language. Below are legal's suggested edits to be fed back to Hightower. I'm including inline clause drafts you can paste into the order form.

-- OUTPUT / PRODUCTIZATION (proposed replacement) --
Customer Content and Customer Output. "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content. Customer Output (the content generated by the Services in response to Customer Content) shall be owned by Customer to the extent Customer is able to establish ownership under applicable law; otherwise, Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable, sublicensable, irrevocable license to use, copy, modify and create derivative works of Customer Output for any purpose, including commercial productization."

Notes: We avoid a blanket assignment (which raises third‑party model IP issues). The license above is effectively assignment for most practical purposes while preserving Redwood's ability to protect model IP.

-- TRAINING / MODEL REUSE (proposed clause) --
No Training Without Consent. "Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Customer Output to train, improve, or otherwise develop models that are used to provide services to third parties without Customer's prior written consent. For Hosted services, Customer may opt into training via the Service console or in writing; for Dedicated and Private deployments, the default is no-training and any change requires a documented agreement."

-- FEEDBACK / TELEMETRY (proposed clause) --
Feedback and Operational Telemetry. "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use De-identified Feedback and Operational Telemetry for the sole purpose of improving Redwood's infrastructure and Services. De-identified Feedback excludes Customer PII and any data specifically designated by Customer in Writing as Confidential. Redwood shall not associate De-identified Feedback with Customer identity for the purpose of training customer-facing models without prior notice and consent."

-- DERIVATIVE FLAGGING (operational note) --
We can add a JSON metadata header on the response payload: {"derived_from_third_party": boolean, "provenance_note": string}. Implementation lead time: ~2 sprints to add opt-in, 1 sprint for full UI exposure and audit logs. If Hightower needs earlier, we can provide a temporary header via our API gateway.

Next steps: Rachel/Ben, send Alicia these three clauses and offer the temporary header approach. If they push for full assignment language, escalate to me and I'll prepare escalation memo for Execs.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@hightower.ai>
Cc: Mark Patel <mark@hightower.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines: output entitlement & training concerns — proposed edits and next steps

Alicia — thanks for patience while we dug in. Below is the consolidated position from Redwood (legal + product). I've pasted the three proposed clause drafts as requested — these reflect a compromise that preserves your ability to productize outputs while protecting Redwood's model IP and allowing operational telemetry for quality.

1) OUTPUT: Proposed language (see attached in the doc we shared). In practice, this gives Hightower the commercial rights you need without a formal assignment that could trigger third‑party IP claims.

2) TRAINING: Default no-training for Dedicated/Private. Hosted offers an explicit opt-in toggle + audit logs (we will provide logs showing opt-in actions). Please confirm whether your legal team requires a signed addendum for opt-ins or if a console setting is sufficient evidence.

3) FEEDBACK: We will accept a limited de-identified telemetry license and provide an operational carveout for bug fixes/security investigations. If Hightower needs no-use at all, we can offer a paid feedback-lockbox add-on — Ben can share pricing.

4) DERIVATIVE FLAGGING: We can provide a temporary response header this week for your engineers and a formal metadata field in the API within two sprints. If you want UI visibility, add one more sprint for console exposure.

Attached: RKim_proposed_response_v1.docx with the clauses formatted for copy/paste. Also re-attaching Hightower_redlines_v2.docx with our inline comments.

Next steps: 
- Alicia/Mark: confirm acceptance of the three clause drafts (or flag specific changes) by 2028-07-24 so we can get procurement and legal signoff.
- Ben: will send a short pricing addendum for feedback-lockbox if Hightower wants absolute no-use.
- If accepted, we'll route final order form via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/HWT-4821-orderform

Happy to hop on a quick call — available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Best,
Rachel
Senior PM, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
